title: Launcher experiment: run the Rust and Vitest FULL stages concurrently on DL560 with isolation (save ~11 min per FULL)
outcome: On DL560 only, a full launcher run executes its Rust-test and Vitest stages concurrently under one run id, with per-stage isolation, and produces results identical to the sequential run on the same commit while finishing measurably sooner. Windows and Central keep sequential stages.
acceptance: A design note names every shared resource between the two stages (ENGRAM_HOME, temp dirs, ports, Git/engram fixtures, CARGO_TARGET_DIR, process groups) and how each is isolated or serialized, including the node behavior group that spawns git/engram (known to interfere: Central test-5f2735f7 55/1).

The concurrent mode is opt-in, limited to Linux/DL560, keeps one aggregated result with per-stage logs and exact source_id before/after, disables fail-fast so diagnostics stay complete, and leaves Windows/Central behaviour unchanged.

On one frozen commit, a sequential and a concurrent run give identical per-stage results and source_id with zero new failures; the measured elapsed saving is recorded; no test is weakened, retried or given a longer timeout.
